scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service canceled 34 days ago, which is outside the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Aaliyah Washington and I'm 80. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello Ms. Washington. I'm sorry to hear about the confusion regarding your billing while you were traveling. To look into this for you, could you please provide your account number and the email address associated with the service?
My account number is 8829-4410 and my email is a.washington@email.com.
Thank you. Just for security purposes, can you please confirm the billing zip code on file as well?

Perfect, thank you. I see the account here. Per our standard Terms of Service, Section 4.2, refund requests must be submitted within 30 days of the charge date. Since you are at 34 days, I am slightly limited in what I can do automatically.
I understand the policy, but I really didn't use the service during that time since I was away. Is there any way to make an exception?

I understand your situation. Because you are just outside the window, I can go ahead and process a one-time courtesy refund for you today. I have initiated that request, and you should see the funds returned to your original payment method within 3-5 business days.

resolution_summary: The agent processed a one-time courtesy refund despite the request falling outside the 30-day policy window.
